name: Aye Finance Ltd
title: Aye Finance Ltd - 544699 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Aye Finance is a micro-MSME NBFC where credit costs fell for a fifth straight quarter to 4.3% and PAR X improved to 6.9%, but FY27 guidance of 3.5–4% credit cost and 25–30% AUM growth is management's own framing rather than hard supply evidence.

triggers.label: Credit costs 4.67% → 4.3% (5th straight cut)
triggers.quote: Credit costs also reduced to 4.3% in quarter 4 compared to 4.67% in previous quarter, which is a 37 basis points reduction quarter-on-quarter.

triggers.label: Borrowing cost to fall 25–35 bps in FY27
triggers.quote: we do expect a borrowing cost to reduce by 25 to 35 basis points compared to FY27.

triggers.label: Q4 disbursements up 26% QoQ to ₹1,655 cr
triggers.quote: disbursements for quarter 4 grew at 26% sequentially to INR1,655 crores of disbursement in the quarter.

triggers.label: Mortgage PAR 90 at 2.7%, rising
triggers.quote: the PAR 90 for the mortgage today is about 2.7% of the total portfolio. This has increased compared to the December quarter.

guidance.value: 25 to 35 bps (later corrected to ~30 bps from 10.87%)

red_flags.label: Mortgage PAR 90 rising to 2.7%
red_flags.quote: the PAR 90 for the mortgage today is about 2.7% of the total portfolio. This has increased compared to the December quarter.

red_flags.label: Credit cost guidance relies on NPA pool resolution
red_flags.quote: The other big piece is the settlement part of the resolution that we will focus on.

red_flags.label: Fair value gains flattering Q4 non-interest income
red_flags.quote: the fair value change that you are seeing is primarily driven on two aspects.

evasions.topic: Sustainability of Q4 fair value gains
evasions.quote: we intend to move it down to OCI because that is where the real line is

summary.headline: Aye Finance Q4 FY26 profit rose 100% QoQ to INR86 crore, with credit cost down to 4.3% and FY27 guidance of 25-30% AUM growth.
summary.overview: Aye Finance closed FY26 with AUM of INR7,044 crore (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ) and Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (up 26% QoQ). Q4 profit was INR86 crore, up 110% YoY and 100% QoQ, with FY26 profit up 13% to INR194 crore. Asset quality improved for a fifth straight quarter, with credit cost at 4.3%, PAR X at 6.9% and GNPA at 4.77%. Management guided FY27 to 25-30% AUM growth, 3.5-4% credit cost, 8.25-8.75% opex ratio and 4-4.5% ROA, with borrowing costs expected to fall 25-35 bps.

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage is 23% of portfolio vs 12% in FY24; PAR 90 at about 2.7% (up vs December quarter), PAR X at about 4.1%, with a target PAR 90 of 2-2.5%. Book is about INR1,500-1,600 crore per management, versus INR1,300-1,400 crore in an analyst's figure.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Secured hypothecation is about 40-47% of book (figures differed in the call) and unsecured hypothecation about 37%. Unsecured HL is said to behave like the secured book; management sees yields stable.

segments.name: CGFMU-covered book
segments.commentary: Roughly INR500 crore of hypothecation book is covered under CGFMU as of March 2026; the company has not used CGTMSE.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30%; opex growth of about 15% is expected to support this.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with Q4 FY27 expected at 3-3.25%; three-year asset quality target 3.25-3.75%.
Opex ratio to fall to 8.25-8.75% in FY27 from 9.6% in FY26; three-year opex guidance about 7-7.5% per analyst's reading.
ROA target of 4-4.5% with leverage of 4-4.5x (total assets to borrowings) and ROE in the high teens; management says this is reachable within FY27.

Borrowing cost expected to fall 25-35 bps from the FY26 level (management later clarified from the Q4 blended 10.87%), driven by replacing high-cost debt, a possible rating upgrade from A stable and partly offset by rising rates.
PAR X to fall to 5.5-6% over FY27 (about 100-150 bps), with about 30 bps in H1. Profit split expected at 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.
capex_capacity: Presence in 18 states and 3 union territories with 571 branches, 6.40 lakh+ active borrowers, and 70+ business clusters; branches are mainly Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.
FY26 staffing rose 17-18%; mortgage manpower rose about 30% and collections team about 70%. FY27 manpower growth is expected to normalise to about 10%, mostly in branch sales and collections.
Collections capacity is to be redeployed to clean up NPA and write-off portfolio.
Management plans at least one new product launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), with market research due by end of Q1.
Mortgage share targeted at 30-35% of the portfolio over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Management says the micro-MSME segment is recovering, with rural consumption and formalisation supporting working-capital demand; April collections are not materially different from Q4 and April disbursements are seasonally lower.
Yield on hypothecation loans is stable; the blended yield falls as mortgage share rises, offset by lower cost of borrowing.
Management says it is not seeing a West Asia impact in March data, and the customer base is not linked to organised supply chains.
Collection efficiency: non-OD CE improved from 99.1% in Oct-25 to 99.5% in Mar-26; Bucket 1 CE rose from 51.8% to 62.5%. Stage 2 (30+60 DPD) is 1.12% of the portfolio.
Competition was not discussed in depth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the product mix changing, and what is the target secured/unsecured split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is 23% of book, target 30-35% in 2-3 years. Balance is hypothecation, with about 40% secured and about 30% unsecured. Management says 96% of customers own residential or commercial property.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM flat in FY27 guidance despite the equity raise and lower cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says mortgage mix lowers yield, offset by replacing old debt at 10.13% incremental cost, worth 30-35 bps. Q3 NIM was 14.2% and Q4 16.4%, mostly from lower borrowing costs and less borrowing after the IPO. NIM is guided to stay level.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: The NPA pool still bulges from early crisis slippages; more than 70% is provided in the hypothecation NPA book. Credit cost should decline from Q2-Q3 FY27, reaching 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27. Stage 3 PCR is to stay above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from fair value gains on mutual funds and a cross-currency swap impact. The net effect is about INR10-11 crore. The company plans to move these fair value items to OCI from April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mortgage PAR 90 and sustainable GNPA levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage PAR 90 is about 2.7%, up from December, with PAR X at 4.1%. Target PAR 90 is 2-2.5% and credit cost below 2% on the mortgage book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing maturity profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings fall due in the next 12 months, at an average cost of about 10.95%, which management describes as relatively expensive debt.

risks_watch: Credit cost path depends on collection efficiency holding and on resolution of the NPA pool; FY27 credit cost guidance of 3.5-4% depends on this.
Rising market interest rates could offset the 25-35 bps borrowing-cost decline; management says priority-sector status limits the impact.
Mortgage PAR 90 rose QoQ to about 2.7%; the mortgage book is new and its credit cost is still elevated.
The opex ratio must fall from 9.6% to 8.25-8.75% while AUM grows 25-30%.
Possible rating review from A stable could lower borrowing costs, but timing is not specified.
Management did not give a timeline for a new product launch beyond end-Q1 market research.
summary.management_tone: Confident and constructive on asset quality, profitability and FY27 targets, with the company citing the guidance as conservative. Less precise on some numbers, with corrections made on the cost of borrowing base and secured/unsecured splits.
key_quotes: Our expectation is that for the guidance would be that for FY26, we will target a growth in the range of 25% to 30%.
we expect to be guided in our workings on a 3.5% to 4% credit cost, supported by better portfolio quality and sustained collection efficiencies.
So we strongly believe that the opex can be brought down to the 8.25% to 8.75%
Our PAR X or PAR 1 plus, whatever you want to call it, stood at 6.9%, improving from 7.6% in quarter 3 of FY26.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.67% in Q3, down 37 bps QoQ

adds.what: New product launch (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others); not a physical capacity addition

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30% (midpoint 27.5%), backed by Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (+26% QoQ) and planned manpower growth of about 10%, but no specific new capacity or order book was quantified; the 571-branch network is existing, and the only new item is an unsized product launch.
